prompt:
以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
As of September 2026, a quiet change is appearing in how some young Japanese people think about travel.

The question may no longer be only, “How many famous places can I see?”

For many young travelers, especially young men, another question is becoming important:

“Can I spend the trip in my own way?”

A 2025 survey found that men aged 29 and under showed strong interest in solo travel and trips built around a personal hobby. Each choice was selected by about one in four respondents.

Another survey found that about 90 percent of Japanese Gen Z respondents wanted free time during an overseas tour. About four in five wanted at least half a day of free time.

Together, these findings point to a growing wish for control, choice, and less pressure during a trip.

But the calendar tells a different story.

When people were asked what they would do if they could take a month off, the most common answer was a trip of about one week. It was chosen by about 24 percent.

However, among people planning an autumn trip, the reported stay was much shorter. The average was about two nights, and the median was two nights.

A government tourism white paper also says that longer stays and more trips are still policy goals. So the country has not fully moved from sightseeing tours to slow, extended travel.

There is another important limit to the story. Among women aged 29 and under, visiting famous tourist sites remained popular, at about 45 percent.

This is not a complete change from one travel style to another. It is a gap between what some young people want from travel and how long they currently stay.

【Point One】
Slow travel can also mean control over time and attention. Even a two-night solo trip built around a personal interest may express this wish more clearly than a longer tour packed with fixed plans. That suggests flexible schedules, free blocks, and hobby-based options may matter as much as longer packages.

【Point Two】
The one-week answer under a month-long break shows possible demand, not normal behavior. Since travel is often linked with having extra time and money, the next challenge is to make slower experiences possible in smaller steps. Success would mean trips becoming more frequent or longer, not just stronger survey interest.

point_one.reasoning: Full Storyの「自分で選べる旅行を望む」という傾向を、二泊程度の趣味中心の旅行にも当てはまる「時間と注意のコントロール」として具体化している。さらに、柔軟な日程や自由時間、趣味別の選択肢が旅行商品に重要だという実務的な示唆を加えており、単なる要約ではない。

point_two.reasoning: 一か月休める場合の「一週間」という回答が実際の通常行動ではない点を踏まえ、時間と費用の制約下でスローな旅行を小さな段階から実現する必要性を示している。旅行の成功を、関心の強さではなく旅行回数や滞在期間の伸びで測るという具体的な評価軸も加えている。
